transcript: In Japanese communities old legends remain Fox, Tanuki, Kappa, Tengu, demons of hell Stories about them have been passed down since childhood These yukai are not mere products of imagination They embodied the wisdom of our ancestors Used to explain natural phenomena The fox is set to be the messenger of the deity Inari Like a servant of the shrine, fox statues guard the entrance The cup-eye is set to live near rivers It has a dish on its head filled with water Adults would urge children, be careful at rivers The Tengu lives in mountainous regions and has a red face and a long nose It would test mountain ascetics These stories taught children awe and fear of nature They emphasize that humans cannot rule nature Today, Uki have become characters in manga and anime Pokemon and spirited away bear strong influence from Japanese yukai culture As traditional customs are being lost through urbanization, yukai continue to live in new forms They are a source for the imagination of creators Even in the age of rationalism when everything seems explainable We have not lost our sense of the invisible At night, walking a mountain path One suddenly turns and feels something is there That sense is the core of Japanese yukai culture you

segments.text: In Japanese communities old legends remain
Fox, Tanuki, Kappa, Tengu, demons of hell
Stories about them have been passed down since childhood
These yukai are not mere products of imagination
They embodied the wisdom of our ancestors
Used to explain natural phenomena
The fox is set to be the messenger of the deity Inari
Like a servant of the shrine, fox statues guard the entrance
The cup-eye is set to live near rivers
It has a dish on its head filled with water
Adults would urge children, be careful at rivers
The Tengu lives in mountainous regions and has a red face and a long nose
It would test mountain ascetics
These stories taught children awe and fear of nature
They emphasize that humans cannot rule nature
Today, Uki have become characters in manga and anime
Pokemon and spirited away bear strong influence from Japanese yukai culture
As traditional customs are being lost through urbanization, yukai continue to live in new forms
They are a source for the imagination of creators
Even in the age of rationalism when everything seems explainable
We have not lost our sense of the invisible
At night, walking a mountain path
One suddenly turns and feels something is there
That sense is the core of Japanese yukai culture
